output.title: Design against vendor price changes before they land
output.body:
Vendor prices change. The useful question is not whether that happens, but which tools in your workflow should trigger a review before the increase starts hurting the business.

For a small business, keep this bounded. Pick one recurring process where a vendor cost matters every week or month: invoicing, customer inquiry triage, or data entry. Then ask one practical question: if this subscription goes up, do I keep it, switch it, or redesign the step?

That is the decision. Not a strategy essay, just a control.

My next-step suggestion is simple: make a one-page vendor list. Mark the subscriptions that are business-critical, note the current rate, and set a review trigger for each one. The trigger can be a renewal notice, a quarterly check, or a budget threshold you choose. When the trigger fires, decide in advance whether the owner gives manual approval, starts a replacement search, or pauses the spend.

If the workflow is repetitive and the cost is easy to trace, that gives you a cleaner boundary than hoping the increase will stay small. Price changes are less annoying when they have to go through a process.
